intro: Israel is small but varied, with a Mediterranean coast, green hills in the north and the Negev desert covering more than half of the land.

chapters.title: From snow to desert
text: The coastal plain holds most of the people and cities like Tel Aviv and Haifa. In the north are the hills of Galilee and the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake. The south is the Negev desert, reaching down to Eilat on the Red Sea.
The Jordan River runs south into the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land on Earth, about 430 m below sea level.

chapters.title: Water
text: Water is scarce, so Israel became a leader in drip irrigation and desalination, turning seawater into drinking water. Much of its tap water now comes from the sea.

chapters.title: Climate
text: Summers are long, hot and dry; winters are mild with most of the rain. Snow sometimes falls in Jerusalem.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing salt from seawater to make fresh water.
